पश्चिमी विक्षोभ का असर: हरियाणा-दिल्ली में बारिश और ठंडी हवाओं का दौर, नवंबर की शुरुआत में दिखेगा बड़ा बदलाव
पश्चिमी विक्षोभ के प्रभाव से महेंद्रगढ़ जिले सहित हरियाणा और दिल्ली-एनसीआर में मौसम बदल गया है, जिससे बूंदाबांदी और तापमान में गिरावट दर्ज की गई है।
HighLights
महेंद्रगढ़ में पश्चिमी विक्षोभ से बूंदाबांदी, तापमान गिरा।
हरियाणा, दिल्ली-एनसीआर में मौसम परिवर्तनशील, ठंड बढ़ेगी।
नवंबर में फिर सक्रिय होगा पश्चिमी विक्षोभ, वर्षा संभव।
जागरण संवाददाता, नारनौल। पश्चिमी विक्षोभ के प्रभाव से महेंद्रगढ़ जिले में मौसम का मिजाज बदल गया है। शनिवार सुबह जिले के कुछ हिस्सों में छिटपुट बूंदाबांदी दर्ज की गई। दिनभर बादलों की आवाजाही के बीच तापमान में भी गिरावट देखने को मिली।
मौसम में आए इस बदलाव से आने वाले दिनों में हल्की ठंड बढ़ने की संभावना है। वहीं, हवाएं शांत रहने पर बूंदाबांदी वाले क्षेत्रों में सुबह के समय हल्की धुंध भी छा सकती है।
राजकीय कालेज नारनौल के पर्यावरण क्लब के नोडल अधिकारी डॉ. चंद्रमोहन के अनुसार, पश्चिमी मौसम प्रणाली के प्रभाव से हरियाणा, एनसीआर और दिल्ली में मौसम परिवर्तनशील बना हुआ है।
शनिवार को महेंद्रगढ़ जिले में सुबह बिखराव वाली बूंदाबांदी हुई, जबकि दोपहर बाद प्रदेश के पश्चिमी हिस्सों में तेज हवाओं, आंधी और हल्की वर्षा की गतिविधियां दर्ज की गईं। कुछ स्थानों पर छिटपुट ओलावृष्टि भी हुई। प्रदेश के कई हिस्सों में दिन और रात के तापमान में गिरावट आई है और तापमान सामान्य से नीचे बने हुए हैं।
रविवार को भी उत्तरी जिलों में रहेगा असर
डॉ. चंद्रमोहन के अनुसार, मौजूदा मौसम प्रणाली का असर रविवार को भी हरियाणा के उत्तरी जिलों में देखने को मिल सकता है। उत्तरी पर्वतीय क्षेत्रों में हल्की बर्फबारी होने के कारण आने वाले दिनों में हरियाणा, एनसीआर और दिल्ली के तापमान में और गिरावट की संभावना है। महेंद्रगढ़ जिले में भी मौसम में उतार-चढ़ाव बना रह सकता है। सुबह के समय हल्की धुंध और ठंड का अहसास बढ़ने की संभावना है।
नवंबर की शुरुआत में भी बदल सकता है मौसम
मौसम विशेषज्ञ के अनुसार, अक्टूबर के अंतिम दिनों और नवंबर की शुरुआत में एक बार फिर पश्चिमी विक्षोभ सक्रिय होने की संभावना है। इसके प्रभाव से हरियाणा, एनसीआर और दिल्ली में मौसम में बदलाव के साथ वर्षा की गतिविधियां हो सकती हैं। इससे क्षेत्र में हल्की ठंड की शुरुआत होने के आसार हैं।
मौसम में लगातार हो रहे बदलाव के बीच जिले में दिन और रात के तापमान पर नजर रहेगी। आने वाले दिनों में तापमान में गिरावट और सुबह की धुंध के कारण मौसम का असर अधिक महसूस हो सकता है।

title: ‘Bungang araw’ now comes with benefits - Daily Tribune
search_term: (heatstroke OR "heat stroke" OR sunstroke OR "heat exhaustion" OR "heat-related death" OR "heat casualty" OR "heat fatality" OR "suspected heat death" OR dehydration OR "heat cramps" OR "heat illness") Andaman and Nicobar Islands
full_text:
You — yes, you — may be compensated for “bungang araw” or heat rash.
This as the Department of Labor and Employment (DoLE) has issued guidelines clarifying which heat-related illnesses may qualify for compensation under the Employees’ Compensation Program during El Niño and other periods of extreme heat.
Labor Advisory 19, Series of 2026, signed by Secretary Francis Tolentino over the weekend, covers the prevention, documentation and reporting of occupational heat-related illnesses, as well as the filing and evaluation of compensation claims.
The guidelines apply to workers covered by the program through the Social Security System and Government Service Insurance System who are exposed, or may reasonably be expected to be exposed, to excessive heat in the workplace. This includes both indoor and outdoor workers.
Aside from heat stroke, heat cramps and heat exhaustion, which are already recognized under existing compensation rules, other illnesses associated with extreme heat may also qualify for compensation under Employees’ Compensation Commission Board Resolution 26-10-40, Series of 2026.
These include heat syncope, or fainting and dizziness; heat rash, or bungang araw; rhabdomyolysis, or muscle damage; dehydration resulting in kidney injury; and neurological disorders affecting the normal functioning of the nervous system.
Whether an illness is work-related will depend on factors such as the employee’s duties, workplace conditions, duration and intensity of heat exposure, protective clothing and equipment, and preventive measures.
Heat Index classifications issued by the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration may also support a claim.
Employers must maintain records of work-related heat illnesses and assist affected workers or their beneficiaries in filing compensation claims.
Supporting documents may include occupational safety and health records, workplace temperature measurements, work schedules, physical workload and work-rest arrangements, records of preventive measures, and witness statements.
Employers must also comply with DoLE reporting requirements, including submitting a Work Accident/Illness Report when required.
The Employees’ Compensation Commission, through its Regional Extension Units, and DoLE, through its regional offices and attached agencies, will disseminate the guidelines and provide technical assistance.

title: Heavy rains to lash Keralam as Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal brew twin storm threats; red alert issued for five districts - The South First

full_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert in five districts of Keralam for October 25 and 26, as a low-pressure system over the Arabian Sea and a developing cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal are likely to intensify rainfall across the state.
Malappuram, Kozhikode, and Wayanad are under a red alert on October 25, while Idukki and Palakkad have been placed under a red alert on October 26. Extremely heavy rainfall exceeding 204.4 mm in 24 hours is likely at isolated places in these districts.
An orange alert has been issued for Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Palakkad, and Kannur on October 25. On October 26, the alert will cover Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Ernakulam, Thrissur, and Malappuram. Isolated areas in these districts are likely to receive very heavy rainfall ranging from 115.6 mm to 204.4 mm within 24 hours. A yellow alert has been issued for Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Alappuzha, and Kasaragod on October 25; Thiruvananthapuram, Kollam, Alappuzha, Kozhikode, and Wayanad on October 26; and Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Palakkad, and Malappuram on October 27. Isolated heavy rainfall of 64.5 mm to 115.5 mm is expected in these districts.
A low-pressure area over the southeastern Arabian Sea and the adjoining Lakshadweep region is contributing to the weather system. The trough extending from the associated cyclonic circulation passes through Keralam and reaches the coast of northern Tamil Nadu. Meanwhile, a well-marked low-pressure area over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a depression on October 24 and move west-northwestward. It is expected to strengthen into a deep depression by October 25 and develop into a cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by the morning of October 26. The system is likely to intensify further and move toward the central-western Bay of Bengal, near the Andhra Pradesh coast, by the morning of October 28.
The IMD has warned that extremely heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places in Keralam on October 25 and 26. Rain accompanied by thunderstorms and strong winds of 30–40 km/h is also possible at isolated places from October 24 to 27.
The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) has issued a warning regarding the possibility of Kallakkadal, or swell surge, along the Keralam coast.
High waves measuring 0.8 to 1.2 metres are likely along the Thiruvananthapuram coast, from Kappil to Pozhiyoor, until 11:30 PM on October 25.
A similar warning has been issued for the Kanyakumari coast, where waves reaching 1.0 to 1.2 metres are possible until 11:30 PM on October 24. Fishermen and coastal residents have been advised to exercise caution due to the possibility of high waves and sea surges.

Hyderabad: Telangana is likely to receive heavy to extremely heavy rainfall on October 28, under the influence of Cyclone Arnab that is developing storm over the Bay of Bengal. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for Khammam, Bhadradri Kothagudem and Mulugu, warning of isolated extremely heavy rain in these districts.
In its forecast on Saturday, the IMD said heavy to very heavy rainfall was likely at isolated places in Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mahbubabad, Warangal, Hanamkonda and Suryapet districts. Heavy rain was also forecast in parts of Mancherial, Rajanna Sircilla, Karimnagar, Peddapalli, Jangaon, Nalgonda, Siddipet and Yadadri Bhuvanagiri districts.
The warning came as a well-marked low-pressure area over the Bay of Bengal was expected to intensify into a cyclonic system, to be named Arnab (ocean), a name contributed by Bangladesh. According to IMD-Hyderabad head scientist S. Stella, the system is likely to become a depression on Saturday, a deep depression on October 25 and a cyclonic storm over the west-central Bay of Bengal by the morning of October 26.
“The system is expected to move west-northwestwards and reach the west-central Bay of Bengal near the Andhra Pradesh coast around the morning of October 28. Its proximity to the coast and continued movement towards the west-northwest are expected to increase rainfall activity across Telangana, particularly in the eastern and southern districts,” she explained.
Residents in low-lying areas were advised to remain alert to the possibility of waterlogging, overflowing streams and disruption to road connectivity. Farmers and commuters have also been urged to monitor local weather advisories, especially as thunderstorms and strong winds may accompany the rain.
On October 27, isolated thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds of 30-40 kmph are likely in several districts, including Khammam, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Mulugu, Nalgonda, Suryapet, Mahbubabad, Warangal, Hanamkonda and Jayashankar Bhupalpally.
For October 29, the IMD has forecast isolated heavy rain in parts of eastern Telangana, including Khammam, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Mulugu, Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Warangal, Hanamkonda, Mahbubabad, Nalgonda, Suryapet and Mancherial. Thunderstorms with lightning and gusty winds of 30-40 kmph are also likely at isolated places across the state.
Hyderabad is expected to have partly cloudy skies and morning haze over the next 48 hours, with temperatures likely to remain around 33°C during the day and 21°C at night.

title: Bay drama may boost city’s rain chances before a monsoon break - The Times of India
search_term: ("heat advisory" OR "heat action plan" OR "heat alert" OR "IMD warning" OR "IMD alert" OR "red alert" OR "orange alert" OR "yellow alert" OR "NDMA advisory" OR "cooling shelter" OR "relief measures" OR "heat compensation" OR "severe weather warning") Andaman and Nicobar Islands
full_text:
Chennai: A drama could unfold over the Bay of Bengal as brewing cyclone Arnab threatens to pull the low-pressure area hovering over the Arabian Sea into its circulation, potentially bringing more rain to Chennai and neighbouring districts. Weathermen said the interaction could trigger heavier spells from Sunday night to Monday morning, before the city enters a likely break in rainfall.
The
IMD has issued a red alert on Sunday for heavy to very heavy rainfall of 12-20cm in 24 hours for three districts along the Western Ghats, an orange alert for heavy to very heavy rainfall for 14 districts and a yellow alert for heavy rain of 6-12cm in 24 hours for 17 districts, including Chennai, Chengalpet, Kancheepuram and Tiruvallur. On Monday, heavy to very heavy rainfall may be restricted to southern and western districts.
V R Durai, director of the Area Cyclone Warning Centre at RMC Chennai, said the system over the east-central Bay of Bengal would draw the Arabian Sea low-pressure area, potentially bringing heavy rain to Chennai and neighbouring districts on Sunday. A trough extending from the cyclonic circulation associated with the Arabian Sea system towards north coastal
Tamil Nadu could further enhance rainfall.
“The trough will continue to bring rainfall till Oct 26, as it may weaken gradually. After that, dry weather may prevail for a few days,” he said.
From Oct 27 to around Nov 3, moisture is likely to be concentrated around the cyclone as it moves towards the south Andhra Pradesh-north Odisha coast, with landfall expected before it moves northwards towards Gangetic West Bengal. Dry weather may prevail over Chennai during this period, leading to a slight rise in daytime temperatures.
“The temperature may not be that high as it is not the season for that because the Sun has moved south of the equator,” Durai said.
On Sunday, Chennai and its suburbs may receive moderate to heavy rain, with thunderstorms and lightning in some areas. Partly cloudy skies are expected, with maximum temperatures of 31-32°C and minimum temperatures of 25-26°C.
Blogger Pradeep John said the heavier spells could occur from Sunday night to Monday morning. “Then we go into a break in rains,” he said in a series of online posts.
Since Oct 1, Chennai has recorded 278.8mm of rain, around 69% above normal. Kancheepuram has received 163.8mm, around 28% above normal; Chengalpet, 145.2mm, around 4% below normal; and Tiruvallur, 198.9mm, around 48% above normal.
